title: Deep learning model REED links DNA sequence to the destination of plant epimutations
summary: REED, a deep-learning model trained on one methylome, reads a per-CG-site methylation set point from DNA sequence. In pedigrees of seven Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, methylation gains concentrated at high set points and losses at low ones, and the equilibrium implied by their rates matched the set point. The set point also predicted germline epimutations in rice and changes in wild plants and a 330-year-old tree. The inferred rules (cooperation among nearby CG sites and transcription-factor motifs) are shared across flowering plants. Preprint; analysis of existing methylome data.
